keyQuotes: We are all talking about the changes brought by AI, so which human capabilities become more important? I believe it's human judgment and aesthetics. If you don't know how to use AI right now, it's like trying to control your car with a TV remote.
If institutions still fail to recognize this and continue judging people using old methods like credentials, diplomas, and educational backgrounds, they will likely fall behind.
The greatest thing these courses gave me is essentially a standard—a set of standards about how the world works, what is better, and what is excellent.
I probably won't consider going to university. I prefer to gain personal abilities, especially the iteration of my way of thinking, through the 'One Small Step' program.

mainPoints.explanation: The school has a 'One Small Step' program where students can register companies and run business projects. University is not the only exit; graduation standards include securing funding, achieving stable income, or transferring project results.
mainPoints.point: Moonshot Academy offers a 'third path' distinct from the Gaokao and studying abroad: growing through real entrepreneurship and project-based learning during high school.

mainPoints.explanation: Math classes let students retrace the path of discovery taken by mathematicians, philosophy classes offer diverse perspectives, and mandatory honors courses aim to establish an internal standard of 'what is excellence'—capabilities more valuable than problem-solving skills in the AI era.
mainPoints.point: The core of education shifts from knowledge transmission to cultivating judgment, aesthetics, and humanistic literacy.

mainPoints.explanation: Teachers and students call each other 'Guardians' and 'Learners.' Mentors provide long-term companionship, and the house system breaks down grade-level barriers, reducing a utilitarian mindset through low-competition activities like a 'Boredom Competition.'
mainPoints.point: The mentorship and house systems reshape teacher-student relationships and the community ecosystem.

mainPoints.explanation: The elementary phase focuses on Chinese, English, math, arts, and sports, integrating science and society through thematic projects. Middle school introduces technology and design courses, while high school offers nearly a hundred courses and entrepreneurial support.
mainPoints.point: Moonshot's education is systematically designed from elementary school, doing 'subtraction' in lower grades and 'addition' in higher grades.

mainPoints.explanation: His personal experience is proof that 'education doesn't have to be a single path,' and it also reflects the pioneering and experimental nature of Moonshot's philosophy.
mainPoints.point: Founder Wang Xiqiao is himself a sample of a 'super high schooler,' having founded the school at 19 after giving up his place at the University of Southern California.

oneSentenceSummary: This in-depth report explores the innovative educational practices at Beijing's Moonshot Academy, showcasing how it uses project-based learning and real-world entrepreneurship to offer students a 'third path' distinct from the traditional Gaokao and studying abroad in the AI era.
originalTitle: 探访北京探月学校：AI 时代“超级高中生” 、大学外的第三种可能与中国创新教育
summary: This is an in-depth report from Silicon Valley 101 on their visit to Beijing's Moonshot Academy. Through a two-day immersive experience, the article presents a comprehensive view of the school's educational philosophy and practices from the perspectives of its founder, teachers, and students. Founded by 19-year-old Wang Xiqiao, Moonshot Academy aims to cultivate 'individuals with inner abundance and active citizens.' The school has no traditional classrooms or fixed schedules. Its high school phase features the 'One Small Step' program, supporting student entrepreneurship (for example, Jiang Yin's project creating assistive tools for dyslexia has registered a company with a team of over 60 people). The curriculum emphasizes judgment, aesthetics, and humanities, complemented by practical spaces like a design studio and MakerSpace. The middle and elementary schools build foundational skills through project-based learning and a mentorship system. The article also objectively mentions external controversies regarding its high tuition fees and less prominent college admission results. Overall, it presents a cutting-edge exploration of educational transformation in the AI era—not training exam machines or study-abroad candidates, but enabling high schoolers to grow into 'super individuals' through real-world projects.
title: Inside Beijing's Moonshot Academy: 'Super High Schoolers' in the AI Era, a Third Path Beyond College, and China's Education Innovation
